Works in Progress "AI isn't replacing radiologists" residency positions record 2025

sources_considered.why: Detailed 2025 analysis with Hinton's quote, residency, vacancy and salary data.
Reports the New York Times account of Mayo Clinic radiologist headcount growth and Hinton's concession.

receipt.public_excerpt: In 2016, Geoffrey Hinton – computer scientist and Turing Award winner – declared that ‘people should stop training radiologists now’.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the 2016 Hinton statement that Marcus paraphrases.

receipt.public_excerpt: In 2025, American diagnostic radiology residency programs offered a record 1,208 positions across all radiology specialties, a four percent increase from 2024, and the field’s vacancy rates are at all-time highs.

evidence_items.explanation: Record training positions and all-time-high vacancies in 2025 show radiologists were not being replaced.

evidence_items.locator: section 'The first decade of diffusion', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: AI is often limited to assistive use on a small subset of scans in any given practice. And despite predictions to the contrary, head counts and salaries have continued to rise.

evidence_items.explanation: Over the decade since 2016, AI stayed mostly assistive, and radiologist headcount kept rising.

evidence_items.publisher: The Decoder (citing The New York Times)
evidence_items.locator: section 'AI helps with tasks instead of replacing professions', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: the number of radiologists at Mayo Clinic has grown significantly—from around 260 in 2016 to over 400 today. That's a 55 percent increase.

evidence_items.explanation: A heavy user of radiology AI grew its radiologist staff by 55% after 2016.

unresolved_gaps: No exhaustive search for individual radiologists who lost jobs to AI anywhere in the world. The literal 'not one' cannot be fully proven.
